Maria Cardenas: Heads-up, prepping a checklist for private deployment hardening. main items: KMS integration choices, audit forwarding, RBAC tightening, and split-tunnel egress constraints. Anyone with recent onprem notes?
Raj Patel: I ran into kube-proxy iptables oddness last week — want to add a netpol + hostNetwork exception section.
Oliver Ng: +1. Also we should call out vault vs cloud KMS tradeoffs for air-gapped installs. TL;DR: vault needs init/unseal ops, cloud KMS avoids that but requires proxying/egress.
Jane Doe: For audit logs we ended up shipping to an internal syslog endpoint over TLS, then Fluentd -> S3. Tech note: must sign messages and include envelope metadata (tenant id, cluster id).
Maria Cardenas: Good, add envelope fields. Also: RBAC changes — recommendation is least privilege SA per component, deny hostPath by default, and separate admin namespace for ops.
Raj Patel: Quick example netpol snippet I used (works for kube 1.26):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-namespace-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Oliver Ng: Note: for private deploys with split tunnels, we recommend whitelisting only necessary KMS endpoints and the audit collector IPs. Otherwise egress rules get messy.
Taylor Smith: On KMS: if customer wants HSM/KMS on-prem (Thales/AWS CloudHSM co-located), we document a TLS mutual auth flow + pinned certs. For Vault, ensure sealed snapshots are handled in DR plan.
Jane Doe: Vulnerability triage note: when CVE affects an upstream component (e.g., containerd or runc), isolate affected nodes with cordon/drain, apply node-level iptable rule to block plugin traffic, and escalate to infra-team. Add automated runbook snippet?
Maria Cardenas: Yes — include runbook steps, and add a step to rotate service-account keys and KMS wrapping keys for sensitive tenants after any suspected compromise.
Raj Patel: Incident simulation we ran: we intentionally disabled fluentd on one cluster and validated detection via audit log gaps. SecBot picked it up and created alert: "audit-forwarding: gap detected (5m)" — that detection logic is worth copying.
SecBot: ALERT: audit-forwarding gap detected on cluster-prod-3. missing events: apiserver.audit.request.create (since 2601234540).
Oliver Ng: For RBAC change approvals: proposal -> canary cluster -> short TTL canary tokens -> full rollout. Keep a revert script that re-applies previous ClusterRoleBindings.
Jane Doe: Also add telemetry: per-tenant log hashes (HMAC) every hour to detect silent suppression. That helped us catch a S3 writer bug earlier.
Taylor Smith: One operational caveat: if customers enable private KMS via peering, ensure the peering routes are documented and monitored; we had a case where an asymmetry dropped egress.
Maria Cardenas: I'll assemble a short playbook doc from this thread. Action items: 1) Oliver: write Vault vs KMS appendix (due 2601234620). 2) Raj: add netpol examples + cordon/drain snippet (due 2601234605). 3) Jane: audit-forwarding runbook + fluentd fallback (due 2601234610). 4) Taylor: HSM/peering caveats + cert pinning steps (due 2601234620).
